newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen slipping at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen slipping at open.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to slip at the open on Wednesday as lower gold and bonds outweighed an overall market uptrend. * TSE 300's all-time high of 6491.13 is in sight.
Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Wednesday as falling gold prices and weaker bonds outweigh the overall market uptrend.

MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said the past three positive sessions bode well for the market but the picture was clouded by negative activity elsewhere and little help was expected from the Wall Street.

"The problem is today we've got bonds under modest pressure and we've got gold down about US$1.50. The June S&P contract is flat...so that's calling for a quiet open in the U.S. market," Beattie said.
She said today's pull-back should be limited as traders wait for U.S. employment data due on Friday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 26.64 points on Tuesday to 6432.72, in sight of the exchange's all-time high of 6491.13, reached on May 26.
U.S. treasuries opened lower, weighed down by European bond weakness, profit-taking and hedge fund selling. But analysts said market sentiment remained bullish and trading was seen range-bound.
In economic news, Canadian foreign reserve holdings rose US$1.169 million in May to US$21.025 billion from US$20.889 in April. Government operations increased reserves by US$966 million in May.

* Alliance Communications Corp said on Wednesday it was "well positioned for continued growth over the next year." The company reported earnings per share of C$0.53 for the fourth quarter, up from C$0.48 in the year earlier period.
